land.text: Boeotia, where Thebes 'was re-established in 315 BC' by Cassander after Alexander destroyed it in 335 BC

predecessors.note: The pages opened do not date the league's own restoration; the start is the refounding of Thebes, its seat.

land.text: the Boeotian cities, which 'decided to break the treaty with Perseus to side with Rome' in 171 BC; the Boeotian League page: 'Rome dissolved the league in 171 BC'

successors.note: The Thebes page has the league dissolved after the Achaean War of 146 BC (see notes); the free cities passed to Roman protection.

capitals.name: Thebes
capitals.note: Federal council at Thebes (Boeotian League page: each group sent sixty delegates to the federal council at Thebes; 'the leading city of Boeotia was Thebes'). Infobox of the regional unit names Livadeia as the modern capital.

correction.text: Boeotia: the cities of the Boeotian federation round Thebes, refounded by Cassander in 315 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Hellenistic Boeotian League; checked with the gazetteer on 2026-10-19, it draws the 14 cells of Boeotia as Macedonian Empire and Greek City-States (310), Antigonid Dynasty (290), Antigonid Macedonia (230), Greek City-States (10 cells) with Antigonid Macedonia (3) in 200 and Greek City-States (13) in 175, and thebans ends 338. No page gives an area; Boeotia is about 3,500 km2 by the gazetteer (14 cells). The shape holds through the sieges and the Aetolian membership of c. 245, which the ledger carries as events. Status inside the keyframe is carried by the ledger: client of Cassander (macedonian-empire) 315-304, of Demetrius (antigonid-dynasty) 304-301, independent 301-293, Antigonid 291-287, independent 287-245, client of the Aetolian League 245-236, client of Antigonid Macedonia from 236. macedonian-empire keeps Cassander's hold 315-304 (Cassander page: restoring Thebes gave 'a power base for Cassander in Boeotia'), so the league does not hold Boeotia as independent land before 301.

correction.text: Boeotia plus Megara, which 'left [the Achaeans] and joined the Boeotian League' in 223 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Megara joins in 223 (Megara page: 'when the Achaeans lost control of the Isthmus in 223 BC the Megarians left them and joined the Boeotian League'). The disc is a 10 km stand-in for the Megarid because the gazetteer has no 'Megara'; the return to the Achaean League is 203 or 193 on the same page, so this keyframe ends 194 and the ledger carries the 193 alternative.

correction.text: Boeotia again without Megara, which 'secured Megara's return, either in 203 or in 193 BC' to the Achaean League

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Boeotia alone until the league is broken up in 171 (Third Macedonian War page: 'broke up the league of Boeotian cities'). The league is Antigonid-tinted until spring 197 (ledger), then an ally of Rome.

region.text: Boeotia, with Thebes re-established by Cassander (a Cassander power base)

ledger.note: 315: Cassander re-establishes Thebes, the seat of the Boeotian League. 'Following Alexander the Great's death in 323 BC, Thebes was re-established in 315 BC' (Thebes page; the Cassander page puts the rebuilding in 316 and says the decision had 'the realpolitik effect of providing a power base for Cassander in Boeotia'). Boeotia therefore stays inside Cassander's realm: macedonian-empire holds the land until Demetrius drives Cassander from central Greece in 304 (its /ledger/65), and this dossier carries 315-304 as a client relation (next event), not as independent land. No page opened dates the league's own restoration, so the start is the refounding of Thebes.

region.text: Boeotia under Cassander, for whom the rebuilt Thebes was 'a power base'

ledger.note: 315: the Boeotian federation as Cassander's client. Cassander page: restoring Thebes 'had the realpolitik effect of providing a power base for Cassander in Boeotia' (verbatim excerpt; the fetch gives the rebuilding of Thebes in 316 and no year for this sentence). The client status is the researcher's reading of 'power base'; the Cassander page gives no 313-312 fighting in Greece and the Thebes and Demetrius I pages do not say who held Boeotia before 304. This dossier records the relation from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord, as with the Aetolian League below); macedonian-empire draws Boeotia as its own land until 304.

region.text: Boeotia, as Cassander is driven from central Greece

ledger.note: 304: Cassander loses central Greece. Cassander page: 'In 304 BC, his rival Antigonus Monophthalmus sent his son Demetrius Poliorcetes to aid Athens against Cassander'; Demetrius 'succeeded in driving Cassander from central Greece and created a Hellenic League' (verbatim excerpts). The page does not name Boeotia; macedonian-empire /ledger/65 records the 304 loss of Boeotia to antigonid-dynasty on the same reading.

region.text: Boeotia within Demetrius's revived Hellenic (Corinthian) League

ledger.note: 304: Boeotia enters Demetrius's league. Demetrius I page: 'In 304 BC, he returned a second time to Greece as liberator, and reinstated the Corinthian League' (verbatim excerpt); his list of cities seized in 304-303 (Panactum, Phyle, Kechries, Epidaurus, Sicyon, Corinth, Bura, Scirus, Argos, Orchomenus) does not name Boeotia and no page opened says who joined the league. The year is the page's, Boeotia the researcher's reading, as in antigonid-dynasty /ledger/2.

301: Demetrius's hold on Boeotia lapses. A bridge: Demetrius I page, 'Cassander, Seleucus I, Ptolemy I, and Lysimachus defeated the two at the Battle of Ipsus in 301 BC' and 'the Athenians refused even to admit him into their city'; the page has nothing else on Greece until 294-291 and does not mention Boeotia in 301. Mirrors antigonid-dynasty /ledger/10 (301 loss, also confidence 1). Boeotia is then independent until the siege of Thebes (293).

region.text: Boeotia, the zone of Demetrius's sieges of Thebes

ledger.note: 293: Demetrius Poliorcetes besieges Thebes. Thebes page: the city faced 'besiegement by Demetrius Poliorcetes in 293 BC'; a revolt in 292 BC brought a second siege that ended with the walls broken.

region.text: Boeotia, secured by Demetrius after the capture of Thebes

ledger.note: 291: Demetrius takes Thebes. 'He faced rebellion from the Boeotians but secured the region after capturing Thebes in 291 BC.'

region.text: Boeotia secured by Demetrius I of Macedon

ledger.note: 291: Boeotia passes to Demetrius. 'He faced rebellion from the Boeotians but secured the region after capturing Thebes in 291 BC'; the Thebes page adds a final siege after the revolt of 292.

287: Thebes recovers its autonomy. 'The city recovered its autonomy from Demetrius in 287 BC, and became allied with Lysimachus, the king of Thrace, and the Aetolian League.' antigonid-dynasty records no matching loss.

region.text: Boeotia, enrolled in the Aetolian League

ledger.note: c. 245: Boeotia joins the Aetolian League. 'Although enrolled for a short time in the Aetolian League (about 245 BC)'; drawn as a client tint of aetolian-league. The membership ends with Demetrius II's invasion of 236 (Demetrius II page; see the 236 event). aetolian-league (eu-02-a) carries no client tint over Boeotia.

region.text: Boeotia, wrested from the Aetolian-Achaean alliance

ledger.note: 236: Demetrius II takes Boeotia from the Aetolian alliance. Demetrius II page: the Aetolian and Achaean Leagues 'now became allies against the Macedonian power' and he 'succeeded in dealing this coalition severe blows, wresting Boeotia from their alliance'; 'In 236 BC, he invaded Boeotia, making the Boeotians submit immediately' (verbatim). The Boeotian League page says only 'enrolled for a short time in the Aetolian League (about 245 BC)', which sits ill with a membership still running in 236; the end year is the Demetrius II page's 236 and moved here from a confidence-1 bridge at 244.

region.text: Boeotia, whose cities 'submit immediately' to Demetrius II

ledger.note: 236: Boeotia submits to Demetrius II. 'In 236 BC, he invaded Boeotia, making the Boeotians submit immediately.' Mirrors antigonid-dynasty /ledger/30. Recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord).
223: Megara joins the Boeotian League. 'when the Achaeans lost control of the Isthmus in 223 BC the Megarians left them and joined the Boeotian League'.

region.text: Boeotia, brought into the Roman coalition at Thebes

ledger.note: 197 (spring): the Boeotian League leaves the Macedonian side. Second Macedonian War page: 'At the start of spring, Flamininus and Attalus went to Thebes to bring the Boeotian League into the coalition'; Flamininus had 'managed to sneak 2,000 troops into the city' and the assembly had little choice but to side with Rome; the paragraph precedes Cynoscephalae (June 197), so the year is the page's chronology, not a stated number (confidence 2). Winter 197/196: 'conflict had broken out in Boeotia' (the pro-Macedonian Boeotarch Brachylles killed). DISAGREEMENT with antigonid-dynasty /ledger/60 (196, 'with the proclamation'): the page's list of the free communities at the Isthmian Games of May 196 (Corinthians, Phocians, Locrians, Euboeans, Magnesians, Thessalians, Perrhaebians, Phthiote Achaeans) does not name the Boeotians, and the infobox lists the Boeotian League on Macedon's side; antigonid-dynasty's end should move to 197.
193 (or 203): Megara returns to the Achaean League. The Megara page has Philopoemen 'secured Megara's return, either in 203 or in 193 BC'; achaean-league's dossier puts it at 192.

171: Rome besieges Haliartus. In the Third Macedonian War Roman fleet forces besieged Haliartus; '2,500 fighters who had taken refuge in the citadel were sold as slaves'; the main cities 'decided to break the treaty with Perseus to side with Rome'.
171: the fight ends within the year; Thebes 'surrendered without fighting', and the pro-Roman party received it. The page gives no date for the fall of Haliartus beyond the war's first year.

region.text: the Boeotian cities, now free allies of Rome

ledger.note: 171: Rome dissolves the Boeotian League. 'Rome dissolved the league in 171 BC, but it was revived under Augustus'; the Third Macedonian War page: the split 'broke up the league of Boeotian cities as some of them supported Perseus'. The Thebes page has the dissolution after the Achaean War of 146 BC; the Achaean War page: Metellus captured 'Thebes, which had been allied to the Achaeans' and 'All leagues and other political entities were dissolved'.

wars.name: Demetrius Poliorcetes' sieges of Thebes

zones.text: Boeotia; Thebes besieged in 293 and again after the revolt of 292

wars.outcome: Demetrius took Thebes in 291 and 'secured the region' (Demetrius page); the Boeotians recovered autonomy in 287.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article for the sieges; the Thebes page gives 293, 292 and 287, the Demetrius page 291.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Rome defeated Perseus at Pydna in 168; the Boeotian cities split, Haliartus fell in 171 and the league was broken up.
wars.note: Only the Boeotian part is recorded here; the war's other fronts belong to antigonid-dynasty and kingdom-of-epirus.

certainty.note: No page gives the Hellenistic league's frontier; Boeotia is the region between Attica, Phocis, Locris and Euboea and the borders are approximate throughout. The Megarid is a 10 km disc.

notes: Eleven pages; the state has no Cliopatria row, so every keyframe is new. Start 315 is the refounding of Thebes by Cassander (Thebes page 315, Cassander page 316), not a dated restoration of the league; end 171 follows the Boeotian League page and the Third Macedonian War page, while the Thebes page puts the dissolution after 146 and the Achaean War page says 'All leagues ... were dissolved' in 146, so a reader who prefers 146 should extend the last keyframe and move the dissolve (Coronea 'put themselves under the protection of the Senate' in 170, Third Macedonian War page, which fits a loose federation surviving 171). The Achaean War (146) is not listed under wars because it falls after the state's end here. Fix run (2026-10-19, after review): the relations with the overlords are now recorded from this state's side (vassal_* events whose counterpart is the OVERLORD: macedonian-empire 315-304, antigonid-dynasty 304-301, aetolian-league 245-236, antigonid-dynasty 236-197), mirroring antigonid-dynasty /ledger/30 and /60, which record them with the league as counterpart. Boeotia 315-304 is Cassander's (macedonian-empire's) and not independent land: Cassander page, 'a power base for Cassander in Boeotia'. The Aetolian membership ends 236 (Demetrius II page), not at a bridged 244. The Antigonid relation ends in spring 197, not at the 196 proclamation: the Second Macedonian War page's list of the free communities does not name the Boeotians, and has Flamininus bring the Boeotian League into the Roman coalition at Thebes before Cynoscephalae. Not on any page opened and therefore not recorded: Macedonian garrisons after 338, who joined Demetrius's league in 304, the Boeotian alliance with Philip V at Phoenice (205), the 313-312 fighting in Greece (the Cassander page says nothing on it), the date of Megara's return to the Achaean League (Megara page: 203 or 193; the Philopoemen and Achaean League pages do not mention it). Counterpart mirrors needed: antigonid-dynasty /ledger/60 should move to 197 and /ledger/2 and /10 are matched here by the 304 and 301 events (the 287 loss is still missing there); macedonian-empire has no vassal tint for 315-304; achaean-league has the 223 loss but no gain for Megara's return; aetolian-league carries no client tint over Boeotia 245-236. Megara has no gazetteer place name (10 km disc at 23.35 E 38.0 N); Haliartus likewise (15 km disc). Thebes the city-state of 361-338 is thebans.json (ends 338, successor greek-city-states).
